summary: Benign (confidence 0.85). F3 shows 10 sign-ins from Portugal via university VPN vpn-edge-02 on device LT-3104; critics rejected impossible travel, Turkcell ASN anomaly, password spray, and VPN KEV relevance because the Turkey event was a non-interactive mail-sync token and vpn-edge-01 was not used. No compromise signal survived.

findings.claim: Most sign-ins come from PT (10 events)

rejected_claims.claim: Impossible travel: Manisa → Lisbon in 32 min
rejected_claims.reason: critic: premature impossible-travel claim: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the person; the PT sign-ins use university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104

rejected_claims.claim: Suspicious sign-ins from an ASN outside the account's baseline: Turkcell (TR), 1 event(s)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: shared-egress ASN: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from 193.140.10.21 in the last 30 days (threshold 10); this ASN is the organisation's own exit (shared NAT / mail relay), not a new personal network for the user

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.21 looks like shared egress: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from this IP in the last 30 days (threshold 10); failures across many accounts are expected background noise, not a coordinated spray

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 (firmware 22.7R2.3) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: vpn-edge-01 did not carry a sign-in for prof.kaya@aegean.edu; its KEV status is not relevant to this account's exposure

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)

actions.action: Confirm LT-3104 is a university-managed device assigned to prof.kaya and review its sign-in/device compliance posture.
Verify vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 is patched for the listed KEV CVEs and confirm no authentication occurred on vpn-edge-01.
Continue treating 193.140.10.21 as shared organisational egress/mail relay; monitor rather than block based on cross-account failures.
Reinforce MFA and non-interactive authentication awareness; alert only on new devices, locations, or mail-sync anomalies for this account.

limitations: DQ checks could not run; confidence not adjusted for data quality.
F3 confidence is only 0.5 (LIKELY). Assessment relies on sign-in metadata and Critic reasoning; endpoint and mailbox telemetry were not analyzed.

risk.rationale: All suspicious signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu have been rejected with documented critics: the TR event is a non-interactive ExchangeSync token (not a person), the PT sign-ins are university VPN (vpn-edge-02) from known device LT-3104, the Turkcell/shared-egress IP 193.140.10.21 is used by 201 distinct accounts (baseline NAT/mail relay, not a personal network), the 54-account failures are background noise across many accounts not a coordinated spray, and the KEV-listed VPN appliances are either not involved in this account's sign-ins (vpn-edge-01) or already patched for the cited CVEs (vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8). No data-quality conflicts remain. The sole verified finding F3 (LIKELY 0.5, 10 PT sign-ins) is a weak signal fully explained by the known VPN/device baseline, leaving no confirmed account-takeover chain and no exposure requiring human review.
